verification.note: Unit 2 (Solutions) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book pp.65-68, which prints the question and a model answer. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. BOOK GAP (book p.65, VSAQ 10): the printed answer names only the pure solvent to solution case. Flow from a DILUTE solution into a concentrated one is the same process and is the case most application questions use, so it is written here. The book also never says what a semi-permeable membrane is, and never separates osmosis from diffusion; both lines are added.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Osmosis is the flow of solvent molecules
through a semi-permeable membrane from the
pure solvent into the solution, or from a
dilute solution into a concentrated one.

lines.text: Solvent moves to the concentrated side.

steps.why: The solvent is more concentrated on the pure side, so more solvent molecules reach the membrane per second from that side than from the solution side. The net result is a flow towards the solution, and it continues until an opposing pressure balances it.
common_mistakes: Saying the solute moves. In osmosis only the SOLVENT crosses the membrane; the membrane blocks the solute.
Writing that the flow is from the solution into the pure solvent. The direction is the other way, towards the more concentrated side.
steps.memory_tip: Only the solvent crosses, and it moves towards the stronger solution.
steps.margin_note: The two marked ideas are "solvent only" and "through a semi-permeable membrane". Give the direction as well.

Osmosis is the diffusion of the solvent

steps.why: The membrane is what makes the process one-sided: it passes one kind of particle and blocks the other, so only the solvent can move to even out the concentration. Osmosis is therefore diffusion of the solvent through a semi-permeable membrane; without that membrane the solute would move as well and the process would be ordinary diffusion.
common_mistakes: Describing the membrane as fully permeable. It has to block the solute, otherwise there is no osmosis.
Naming a filter paper as a semi-permeable membrane. Filter paper passes both solute and solvent.
steps.memory_tip: Semi means half: only one kind of particle passes, the solvent.
steps.margin_note: One named membrane is enough. The one-line contrast with diffusion is the usual second half of this mark.

insider_note: Osmosis and osmotic pressure are asked as a pair in this book. Osmosis is the flow; osmotic pressure is the push applied to stop it. Answering one with the other loses the whole mark.
